2607.04927.title: DSWAM: A Dual-System World Action Foundation Model for Fine-Grained Robot Manipulation
2607.04927.paper_summary: World Action Models (WAMs) provide a promising alternative to Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies by using video-based world modeling as dense supervision for robot action learning. Existing WAMs excel at physically grounded execution, but typically lack the explicit language-level planning interface in VLM-based VLAs for decomposing coarse instructions. Such decomposition becomes important when household tasks involve complex multi-step goals, where coarse user commands need to be converted into sequences of fine-grained executable subtasks. Meanwhile, the field still lacks a fair real-robot comparison between VLA and WAM execution capabilities, since existing systems often differ in data, robot embodiments, and task protocols. To address both the decomposition gap and the need for a controlled WAM-VLA comparison, we introduce DSWAM, a Dual-System World Action Foundation Model for fine-grained robot manipulation. DSWAM keeps a System 1 WAM executor as the default control path and optionally activates a System 2 vision-language subtask planner only when task decomposition is useful. The planner predicts executable subtasks from short-term visual history and a global task prompt, while the WAM executor performs world-aware action generation for each instruction or subtask. The executor is trained with action prediction and video co-training, but inference directly predicts action chunks without explicit future video generation. To make this execution path practical on real robots, we further integrate TensorRT acceleration, asynchronous execution, and real-time chunking (RTC) so that policy queries do not block robot control. To provide a fair real-robot comparison with VLA policies, we build and evaluate DSWAM under the DeMaVLA real-world deformable manipulation setting with matched robot platform, pretraining data, post-training data, and evaluation criteria.
2607.04927.paper_summary_zh: 世界行動模型（WAMs）通過使用基於視頻的世界建模作為機器人行動學習的密集監督，提供了一種有前景的替代方案來取代視覺-語言-行動（VLA）政策。現有的WAM在物理基礎執行方面表現出色，但通常缺乏VLM基礎的VLA中用於分解粗略指令的明確語言層級規劃介面。當家庭任務涉及複雜的多步驟目標時，這種分解變得重要，因為粗略的用戶命令需要轉換為一系列細緻的可執行子任務。同時，該領域仍然缺乏VLA和WAM執行能力之間的公平實際機器人比較，因為現有系統通常在數據、機器人實體和任務協議上存在差異。為了解決分解差距和對受控WAM-VLA比較的需求，我們引入了DSWAM，一種用於細緻機器人操作的雙系統世界行動基礎模型。DSWAM將系統1的WAM執行器作為默認控制路徑，並僅在任務分解有用時選擇性地啟用系統2的視覺-語言子任務規劃器。該規劃器根據短期視覺歷史和全局任務提示預測可執行的子任務，而WAM執行器則為每個指令或子任務執行世界感知的行動生成。該執行器通過行動預測和視頻共同訓練進行訓練，但推理直接預測行動片段，而不需要明確的未來視頻生成。為了使這一執行路徑在實際機器人上可行，我們進一步整合了TensorRT加速、異步執行和實時分塊（RTC），以便策略查詢不會阻塞機器人控制。為了提供與VLA政策的公平實際機器人比較，我們在DeMaVLA現實世界可變形操作設置下構建並評估DSWAM，並匹配機器人平台、預訓練數據、後訓練數據和評估標準。
